definition: WaveNet is a deep neural network for generating raw audio.
details: It was created by researchers at London-based AI firm DeepMind. The technique, outlined in a paper in September 2016, is able to generate relatively realistic-sounding human-like voices by directly modelling waveforms using a neural network method trained with recordings of real speech. Tests with US English and Mandarin reportedly showed that the system outperforms Google's best existing text-to-speech (TTS) systems, although as of 2016 its text-to-speech synthesis still was less convincing than actual human speech. WaveNet's ability to generate raw waveforms means that it can model any kind of audio, including music.

explainer.lead: WaveNet is a deep neural network for generating raw audio, created by DeepMind and outlined in a September 2016 paper. It generates relatively realistic-sounding human-like voices by directly modelling waveforms, reportedly outperforming Google's best existing text-to-speech systems in tests with US English and Mandarin.

tiers.eli5: Instead of assembling speech from pre-recorded snippets, it learns to paint the sound wave sample by sample, like drawing a curve point by point until it sounds like a person.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers train the network on recordings of real speech and generate audio by modelling the waveform directly. As of 2016 its text-to-speech synthesis still was less convincing than the best alternatives.
tiers.paperLevel: A neural network trained with recordings of real speech that models raw audio waveforms directly, generating samples one at a time. Known limit: as of 2016, synthesis was still less convincing than the best existing systems.

explainer.example: Trained on real speech recordings, the system produced human-like voice audio that beat Google's best existing TTS in US English and Mandarin tests.
